verdict.line: You lose short trades before level 6 when his Q (Volcanic Rupture) into E (Searing Charge) catches you near a wall; you win from level 6 onward once Fury of the Sands is up and your Q stacks start compounding.

brief.thesis: Ornn has the lane and solo-kill edge because his Q (Volcanic Rupture, 800 range) pokes you down before you can even reach him, and his E (Searing Charge) punishes any wall-adjacent trade with a knockup. Nasus has no answer to that at level 1-5 since Siphoning Strike only works at 255 range and needs a kill to scale. The 50.3% head-to-head win rate over 1676 games says this evens out hard once Fury of the Sands and enough Q stacks come online — the matchup is a timing problem, not a losing one.

theirWindow.when: Q lands and you're near terrain
theirWindow.what: If Volcanic Rupture's fissure slows you within range of a wall, back off immediately — Searing Charge colliding with terrain creates a shockwave that knocks you up, and that combo is his entire kill pattern pre-6.

yourWindow.when: Level 6+, his E and R both down
yourWindow.what: Cast W (Wither) first to cut his attack and move speed, then walk in and trade autos plus Q — with Fury of the Sands active you're draining his max health into bonus damage while his only disengage tools are on cooldown.

start.why: The flat damage reduction on proc eats a huge chunk of Ornn's Volcanic Rupture poke, letting you sit in lane and farm Q stacks instead of backing off every time he throws a fissure.

boots.why: Ability haste shortens Siphoning Strike's cooldown (8/7/6/5/4s) and Spirit Fire's flat 12s cooldown, so you're casting both more often per minute — stacks and zone control compound faster than armor ever matters pre-6.

core.why: The on-hit damage and movement speed proc let you close the gap on Ornn faster so your 255-range Q actually connects, and it accelerates how fast your stacks pile up.
Flat armor and ability haste blunt his autos and his Volcanic Rupture / Searing Charge cooldowns, directly answering the Q-E combo that defines his early lead.
Boosted healing stacks with Soul Eater lifesteal, letting you out-sustain his magic damage poke in extended trades once you have stacks to actually hit him with.

situational.when: ornn stacks health and armor and you need to shred his effective HP while punishing any healing he picks up
their team skews heavily toward magic damage and Ornn's poke stops being the main threat
you want the AoE slow proc for splitting side lanes and clearing waves faster once stacks are high

runes.keystoneWhy: The sustain and movement speed on hit let you survive his ranged Q poke phase and reposition out of Searing Charge's dash lane, buying time until your stacks and R come online.

summoners.why: This combo posts the best measured win rate (51.5% over 27.5% pick share) in the matchup, and Ghost specifically lets you dodge the Searing Charge dash window or close distance fast once Wither and R are both up post-6.

playing.title: Farm Q at melee range, patiently
playing.detail: Siphoning Strike is only 255 range, so you have to walk up for every stack — do it on waves, not into his Volcanic Rupture threat range, since getting poked down while stacking is how this lane goes even.

playing.title: Respect walls before 6
playing.detail: Never trade near terrain when his E (Searing Charge) is up — colliding with a wall triggers the shockwave knockup that turns a normal poke exchange into a full combo.

playing.title: Wither before every real trade
playing.detail: Cast W to decelerate his movement and attack speed before committing autos; it both reduces the damage he returns and keeps him from disengaging once you're in range.

playing.title: Zone waves with Spirit Fire
playing.detail: Drop E on the wave or directly under Ornn when he goes to last-hit — the armor reduction boosts your own Q damage on top of the burn, making it a farming and poking tool at once.

playing.title: All-in only post-6 with his CDs down
playing.detail: Wait for Fury of the Sands and for his E and R to be on cooldown before committing — Ornn's solo-kill edge is real before level 6 and disappears once your ultimate is live.

playing.title: Track stack count, not just level
playing.detail: Your actual power spike isn't a level number, it's a stack threshold — once you're past roughly 30-40 stacks your Q damage alone starts winning trades Ornn's kit can't answer.

playing.title: Scale into split push with Teleport angle in mind
playing.detail: Once Trinity Force and Frozen Heart are both up, your stacked Q lets you solo side lanes faster than Ornn can answer — look to translate lane parity into map pressure rather than forcing more trades.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1) — the tactical reasoning connecting them to specific ability timings and trade patterns is this brief's own analysis.

stats.opponentTip: It is important to avoid Ornn’s (Q)-(E) combo. Focus foremost on raising your [Q] stacks, and try go in for the kill post-level 6 when Unsealed Spellbook + Fury of the Sands [R] come off cooldown.
